drhp.business: The Company operates in the Indian jewellery business across wholesale and retail channels, offering antique, diamond and gold jewellery. During the year under review it opened its first branded retail outlet, "RIIVARA by Swarnsarita Jewels", at Mumbai, as its entry point into organised retail. Its customer base spans agricultural-income households as well as service-sector earners and families supported by remittances from members employed outside their home town, which the Company states limits its exposure to any single monsoon season.

risks.note: Management calls the continued gold-price rally — up approximately 50-73% in FY 2025-26 — the most immediate near-term risk to jewellery volume demand. While value-based revenue benefits from higher prices, volume contraction in the mid-market and mass segments can weigh on profitability and working-capital intensity, making forward hedging through MCX and gold metal loan structures increasingly critical to protect margins.
risks.risk: Sustained elevated gold prices and volume pressure

risks.note: US tariff hikes to 50% levels are flagged as a significant headwind for India's gems and jewellery exports, particularly polished diamonds, with the US absorbing over 40% of India's polished diamond exports. The diamond jewellery industry already saw a 15% drop in annual revenues in FY 2024-25 on weak US and EU demand, and trade-policy uncertainty introduces volatility into both exports and domestic supply chains.
risks.risk: Global trade policy and export risk

risks.note: The regulatory environment continues to evolve — new BIS terminology standards for lab-grown diamonds (IS 19469:2025), updates to hallmarking requirements, import duty structures and GST applicability all require continuous monitoring and compliance investment.

Despite structural consolidation the unorganised sector remains formidable in Tier 2, Tier 3 and rural markets. Price sensitivity there constrains the ability of organised players to pass on cost increases, and the regulatory and tax compliance burden creates transitional cost disadvantages relative to unorganised competitors.

Consumer tastes are shifting rapidly under digital exposure, influencer culture and global fashion trends. Management states that failure to anticipate and respond to preference shifts, particularly among Gen Z and millennial segments, carries meaningful revenue risk over the medium term and requires continuous investment in design innovation.
risks.risk: Changing consumer preferences and design obsolescence

risks.note: In November 2025 SEBI issued a public advisory noting that digital gold products are not regulated under existing market frameworks — an emerging segment where UPI-linked purchases tripled during 2025 — so platforms and jewellers active in the space must monitor regulatory evolution closely.

Elevated geopolitical tensions simultaneously drive gold investment demand and constrain consumer sentiment; potential trade slowdowns from US tariff policy and global financial market volatility are flagged as tail risks, with the IMF cautioning that prolonged trade tensions and protectionist policies could dampen the global and Indian outlook.

The Company's own risk-and-mitigation paragraph acknowledges exposure to agricultural-income customers and the vagaries of the monsoon. Management argues the impact is limited because India has two harvest seasons and because much customer income comes from service-sector engagement and from remitters employed outside their home town — a mitigation argument rather than an elimination of the exposure.
